content.question: Which IDE did the instructor recommend for getting started with Kotlin for Android?
content.explanation: He recommended Android Studio as the IDE for Kotlin Android development.
hints: Android Studio is the standard Android IDE

content.question: To create a new Kotlin file in Android Studio the instructor asked you to right-click which package area?
content.explanation: He right-clicked the app package (e.g., com.myandroidworld.myfirstproject) to add a new Kotlin class/file.
hints: Source files belong under the app package

content.question: Which option did he choose from the New menu to create a Kotlin file?
content.explanation: He selected 'Kotlin class/file' from the New menu and then chose the 'file' option.
hints: The New dialog contains Kotlin class/file options

content.question: Which Kotlin file type did he select to create a runnable snippet for quick testing?
content.explanation: He chose the simple 'file' option to create a Kotlin file with a `main` function for quick runs.
hints: A plain file lets you add a main() to run code directly

content.question: What is the purpose of the `main` function in a Kotlin file?

options.text: It acts as the starting point for running the file's code
It is only used in Android manifests

content.explanation: The `main` function denotes where execution starts when running a Kotlin file directly.
hints: Without main(), the file is not runnable as a standalone snippet

content.question: Which run target did the instructor use to run a single Kotlin file instead of the whole app?

options.text: Select the Kotlin file's run configuration (mainKTFile)

content.explanation: He ran the Kotlin file directly by choosing the file's run option (e.g., run mainKTFile) instead of the app target.
hints: The play button context changes to the selected run target

content.question: Where does the output from running a Kotlin file appear in Android Studio?

options.text: The Run window/console at the bottom

content.explanation: He pointed out that the run output appears in the Run window at the bottom of Android Studio.
hints: Run console shows stdout from main()

content.question: What visual indicator showed the file was runnable again after restoring the main function?

options.text: A play/run button appears next to the file in the editor gutter

content.explanation: He noted that when `main` exists the small run/play icon appears next to the code, indicating it's runnable.
hints: Gutter run icons indicate runnable code

content.question: What happens if you remove the `main` function from a Kotlin file used for quick runs?

options.text: The file is no longer runnable and the run button disappears
Android Studio will run it anyway
It converts the file to Java

content.explanation: Removing `main` means there's no entry point; the run button disappears and you can't run the file directly.
hints: main() is the entry point for running a file

content.question: Which Kotlin keyword did the instructor type to start writing a function?
content.explanation: In Kotlin, functions are declared with the `fun` keyword (e.g., `fun main()`).

content.question: When running the Kotlin file the instructor used `println` — what does `println` do?

options.text: Prints the text and moves to the next line

content.explanation: `println` prints text and advances to a new line in the output console.

content.question: What happens if you run a file without a `main` function?

options.text: You get an error because there's no entry point
The file runs with default main
The emulator will run the file

content.explanation: Without `main`, there is no starting point and the IDE cannot run the file as a standalone program.
hints: main is required for runnable files

content.question: What is the difference between the top play button and the small play button next to code?

options.text: Top play runs the app; gutter play runs the specific file or configuration
Both do exactly the same thing
Gutter play builds the entire project

content.explanation: The top run target typically runs the full app, while the gutter/run icon runs the specific file or configuration.
hints: Context matters for which target is run

content.question: Why did the run button disappear when he removed `main` from the file?

options.text: Because there's no runnable entry point without main
Because the file had syntax errors unrelated to main

content.explanation: The run button is shown only when the file contains a valid entry point like `main()` to execute.

options.text: Hello World in the Run console
A popup dialog in the emulator
A new layout file is generated
